moat_against: Pricing power failed: 2023 Runtime Fee reversed after developer revolt; Godot is the free Plan B
Unreal owns AAA/AA high end (GDC 2026: 42% vs Unity 30% primary engine)
Create grows only ~2% YoY — the moat business is not the growth business
Ads challenger, not leader: AppLovin AXON ahead; publisher supply is bought, not owned
No owned consumer surface; hostage to Apple/Google platform rules
GAAP returns on capital still negative
moat_for: Dominant mobile/indie engine installed base with real switching costs
Engine-to-ads flywheel: Create supply and runtime data feed Vector
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat (5/10, CAP 8.5 yrs): the mobile/indie engine installed base carries real switching costs and feeds a unique engine-to-ads data flywheel (Vector >$1B run rate, Strategic Grow +63% YoY in Q2'26), but pricing power failed its one real test (2023 Runtime Fee reversed), Unreal owns the high end, Create grows only ~2%, and in ads Unity is the challenger to AppLovin with supply that is bought, not owned.
name: Unity Software Inc.
one_liner: Real Vector-led turnaround, moat 5/10 — but TTM owner's earnings are just $0.45/share after a $342M SBC bill, so at $46.63 the weighted IRR is 5.0% (IV@15% $7.73); clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$7.73, and even the super-bull case alone clears only below $15.20.
sector: Technology — game engine & mobile advertising software
